To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sorbent-based air filter performance can be predicted using a numerical modeling approach.
the C-MT model can be used to predict filter performance, and the C&D-MT model provides a more accurate prediction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding and modeling of sorbent filter/air cleaner.
the development of a numerical simulation model to predict the performance of sorbent filters.
the modeling, verification and validation of the sorbent-based air filter/air cleaner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C-MT model and C&D-MT model are capable to simulate the fundamental mass transfer and sorption processes, and to predict the filter performance of the sorbent filters for non-industrial applications, and the C&D-MT is more accurate than C-MT.

this study is the first attempt to model the fundamental mass transfer processes in sorbents-based filters, to predict and explain the filter performance based on the fundamental mass transfer mechanisms, to provide a tool for filter design and maintenance.
the C-MT model is able to predict the breakthrough time and breakthrough concentration with good accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a C&D-MT model was developed and verified to simulate the sorption-based filter performance, and it is capable of providing useful information to the design and selection of air cleaners for non-industrial applications.
a new C-MT and C&D-MT models were developed and verified by comparing with experimental data.

we have successfully developed a model that can be used to predict the filter performance for different sorbent-based filter designs, different environmental conditions, and different challenge gas concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-MT model can be used for the preliminary design of sorbent filters, and the C&D-MT model is recommended for the detailed design of sorbents filters.
the C&D-MT model is a good choice for modeling the sorbent-based filter.

the C-MT model is sufficient for the prediction of the filter’s service life, while the C&D-MT model is required to predict the filter’s initial performance and the transient performance during its early stage.
